Resolutions of 1965

20 resolutions, 65% unanimous. Decolonisation.

  • 200 (1965) Admission of Gambia to membership in the United Nations
  • 201 (1965) Extension of the stationing in Cyprus of the UN Peace-keeping Force
  • 202 (1965) Requesting the United Kingdom to take all necessary action to prevent a unilateral declaration of independence for Southern Rhodesia by the minority Government
  • 203 (1965) Inviting the Secretary-General to send a representative to the Dominican Republic
  • 204 (1965) Incursion by Portuguese military forces into Senegalese territory
  • 205 (1965) Calling for a permanent cease-fire in Santo Domingo
  • 206 (1965) Extension of the stationing in Cyprus of the UN Peace-keeping Force
  • 207 (1965) Reaffirming resolution 186 (1964) on the Cyprus question
  • 208 (1965) Election of members of the International Court of Justice
  • 209 (1965) An immediate cease-fire between India and Pakistan
  • 210 (1965) Requesting strengthening of the UN Military Observer Group in India
  • 211 (1965) Demanding immediate cease-fire and subsequent withdrawal of armed personnel
  • 212 (1965) Admission of the Maldives to membership in the United Nations
  • 213 (1965) Admission of Singapore to membership in the United Nations
  • 214 (1965) Demanding that parties observe the cease-fire and calls for prompt withdrawal of military personnel
  • 215 (1965) Calling upon India and Pakistan to schedule troop withdrawal
  • 216 (1965) Calling on all States not to recognize the minority régime in Southern Rhodesia
  • 217 (1965) The proclamation of independence by the minority régime in Southern Rhodesia
  • 218 (1965) The question of Territories under Portuguese administration
  • 219 (1965) Extension of the stationing in Cyprus of the UN Peace-keeping Force

Security Council Record is an independent record of every resolution, vote and veto of the United Nations Security Council since 1946. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the United Nations. For official documents, use the Security Council website and the UN Digital Library.
